t: In the quadrangle of Somerset House stands George III and the River Thames, a Grade I listed bronze group showing the king with Neptune, or Father Thames. The sculptor was John Bacon, and it was erected between 1778 and 1789. Bacon is reckoned the founder of the British school of sculpture and won the esteem of George III. The building around you is by Sir William Chambers, who also created the Gold State Coach and the pagoda at Kew. George III was the first Hanoverian monarch born in Britain.
